name: ref_2
description: Print of a 4-board 3x3 ChArUco sheet, serial ref_2.

printer.note: Scale 100 % and Print Scaling None, and it still came out 4.7 % small. The fault is in Width and Height: the artwork is 4318 x 5588 px at 508 dpi, which is exactly 8.5 x 11 in, and 4318/532.672 = 8.1063 -- so the image is laid down at 532.672 dpi to fit the printable area. Predicted scale 0.95369. See docs/planning/printing-the-target-at-size.md. RESOLVED: the resolution field is locked until 'Ignore Page Margins' is checked. With it checked, Width and Height read 8.5 x 11 and the sheet prints full size. Safe here because PAGE_MARGIN_MM insets everything 15 mm against a 5-6.5 mm unprintable border, so only blank paper is clipped.
printer.axes: Short edge first on US Letter, so the process (feed) axis is 'down' on the sheet, 279.4 mm, and the laser scan axis is 'across'. Fuser shrinkage is usually worse along the process axis, so if the 0.131 per cent residue is the fuser the prediction is sy < sx. ref_2 measured the other way by +0.025 +- 0.105 per cent, which is not significant either way.

_provenance.measured: NOT YET TAKEN. Six caliper readings on each printed span, outer edge to outer edge, WHILE THE SHEET IS STILL INTACT -- after cutting the longest baseline inside one piece is too short to see the print error. See docs/planning/measuring-the-printed-target.md.
_provenance.printer: Record the make and the driver's scaling setting. ref 1 came out 4.75 per cent undersize because 'fit to printable area' was left on.
_provenance.scale: 4.76 per cent undersize, uniform 0.95238 +- 0.00050. The print dialog predicts 0.95369 from its own Width and Height fields, leaving a deficit of -0.131 per cent, 2.6 sigma, which toner spread can only make larger. Laser fuser shrinkage of 0.1 to 0.3 per cent is the right size and sign. ref_1 came out 0.95251 from a different application, so the application is not the variable -- the driver's treatment of the printable area is.
_provenance.anisotropy: -0.025 per cent +- 0.105, 0.2 sigma. Not detected, agreeing with ref_1's +0.057 +- 0.100. Two prints now say this printer has no measurable anisotropy.
_provenance.shear_detected: RESOLVED as none, and the history is the point. Tranche 1 alone gave -0.390 mm against a 2 sigma floor of 0.318 and would have been recorded as detected. Tranche 2 gave -0.040 against 0.256. Pooled, -0.215 against 0.224 -- none. The tranche-1 result rested on a single low reading of 144.28, exactly the artefact that produced and then destroyed ref_1's +0.273 per cent anisotropy.
_provenance.diagonals: DO NOT USE FOR SCALE. They give 0.94766 where the axes give 0.95238, reading 0.471 per cent short; ref_1 read 0.345 per cent short the same way. At 144.8 mm the jaws sit at 95 per cent of travel and splay.
_provenance.uniformity: No drift. Rows differ by -0.137 mm +- 0.221 (0.6 sigma) and columns by -0.108 +- 0.078 (1.4), with the uncertainties taken across sittings. Pooling all twelve readings as if independent put the columns at 2.13 sigma, which is the same over-confidence in a different costume.
_provenance.readings_mm: across #0-#1 came in at sd 0.006 mm -- three readings inside one caliper count. That is not three independent seatings; compare sd 0.191 on the nominally identical #2-#3 span. Release the jaws fully between readings.
_provenance.scale_uncertainty: The sem is computed from the FOUR (span, sitting) group means, not from 24 pooled readings. The between-sitting gaps run to 0.437 mm and reach 5.5 times the within-sitting scatter, so readings inside one sitting are not independent. Pooling them naively would have quoted 0.060 and 0.027 per cent on the two axes -- 1.5 times too confident.

readings_mm._what_was_seated_on: outer edges of the black squares, board to board
readings_mm._tranches: Two sittings of three readings on each span, as the protocol asks. It earned its keep: the between-sitting gaps run to 0.437 mm, up to 5.5 times the scatter within a sitting, and tranche 1 alone reported a shear that tranche 2 dissolved.
